# TUI Test Matrix Card — Windows — 2026-09-21

Scope: `CppTest_Tui` Debug x64, with explicitly identified Debug Win32 supplemental checks, following `.github/Jobs/DebugTuiControlTestSop.md`. This card tracks only the local TUI showcase; remote protocol matrices are out of scope.

## Resumed console verification — 2026-09-21

Completed using owned ConPTY sessions, native console event replay, live cell-buffer capture, real pseudoconsole resize and deterministic regression tests. The rows below distinguish live checks, programmatic alternatives and unavailable backend features. Physical desktop input and Windows Terminal display/profile checks are skipped under the user's instruction. The helper opens inheritable CONIN$/CONOUT$ handles before invoking the repository wrapper; startup paints correctly. Earlier failed helper launches had invalid child standard handles and exited with code3 after their runtime dialogs were captured and dismissed; they do not establish an application defect.

Evidence is retained under `%TEMP%/TuiResume-20260921`: each session contains `actions.jsonl`, numbered console-cell captures (including attributes), raw `output.vt`, and the normal exit result where available. Session names in the table abbreviate the common `20260921-` prefix. Final sessions205312,213843 and214400 all returned normally with exit0; their shell commands produced separate output lines. The owned pseudoconsole shells and helper server are closed.

Pre-fix baseline: the Debug x64 `UnitTest` run passed **93/93 files and 1798/1798 cases**, including all 19 `TestTuiProvider.cpp` cases, with no appended memory-leak report. This covers provider-only pre-Show/viewport geometry, reentrant close/listener removal, hosted-modal interception, queued callbacks, retained palette templates, tab geometry and wide-cell repair. These deterministic tests supplement the live console checks; they do not establish physical terminal input or displayed appearance. Raw output is retained as `UnitTest-1798.log` in the evidence directory. Generated snapshot changes from this run were retained there as a patch and removed from the working tree; no baseline update was intended.

Build and regression results: both-architecture `GacUI_Compiler` completed with exit0 and no UI error files. Debug Win32 and x64 solution builds passed with zero warnings/errors; both Metadata_Generate runs and x64 Metadata_Test passed. Corrected Debug Win32 and x64 UnitTest each passed **93/93 files and 1803/1803 cases**, with no skipped files or appended leak report (`UnitTest-Win32.log`, `UnitTest-x64.log`). The first run stopped at a new test expectation: CDB confirmed redo intentionally selects restored text, so the test now asserts selection and moves the caret before appending. Both runs include all19 TUI provider cases and added caption coverage, timer work and interior/final block-caret rendering. Existing Win32 file-dialog snapshot differences normalize to identical rendered trees apart from the working-directory path; the x64 run leaves only the path difference, which was preserved as evidence and restored. The new five-editor regression snapshots are retained. Integration rebased onto3a8a1ae21; canonical fixes/tests are byte-identical to the tested versions. Resource generation finished again without UI errors, generated binary conflicts were resolved, and both architecture rebuilds/metadata passed. Final incremental builds again passed with zero warnings/errors (`Build-Win32-final.log`, `Build-x64-final.log`). Fixes, generated resources, regressions and fallback guidance are published in `ae8b8504d`.

Native grid reference: rebuilt Debug x64 hosted CppTest, PID24248 on automation port8897, confirmed Name/Website Left/Right and Shift selection with Up/Down unchanged; collapsed Gender/Category navigation retains the value, while expanded arrow/Home/End/Page navigation clamps and Enter/mouse commits. After editor dismissal, grid row navigation resumes. The owned reference process exited normally via `!Exit`; no runtime dialogs. This is comparison evidence, separately from the TUI replay below.

Recycling evidence is recorded separately from resize retention. The fixed Refresh datasets fit at80x25. Tiny7/8-row captures initially clipped the same leading rows despite Home/End input; those frames do not prove scrolling. Both completed full suites include52 matching MakeInvisibleItems/UpdateInvisibleItems/UpdateInvisibleChildItems cases across the shared list/tree fixtures. These tests deliberately scroll20/100-item datasets away, change hidden text/check state, return, and save unchanged regression snapshots. The TUI provider fixture separately retains a40-row list at a nonzero horizontal/vertical offset through every palette. These passing programmatic tests supply recycling coverage without mislabeling unchanged console frames.

Palette regression evidence: the completed TUI provider fixture checks retained document identity, selection, undo/redo availability, nonzero scroll and focus through all six palettes; selected list row20 and offset(30,10); tree expansion; header identity, width60, sort/filter and hover/pressed colors; newly created controls; and one menu action per activation. It also refreshes open content/date dropdowns and a hosted modal, checking that they remain usable. This supplies the queued/open-popup paths that the showcase's main radios cannot reach while modal. The live checks below supplement these precise assertions.

## Issues Found and Fix

Observed label defect: RepeatFlow displayed `eightteen` for18. Corrected the identical English-number conversion in canonical TuiControlTest and FullControlTest XML; regenerated both architectures and verified `eighteen` live. The rich-document emoji clipboard crash reproduced twice. First-chance CDB confirmed the incomplete surrogate run in `GenerateHtmlVisitor` and `UtfGeneralEncoder`; the fix keeps a supplementary character in one insertion/undo record. Live external clipboard, repeated copy and undo/redo retesting passed. Debugger evidence: `document-freeze.log` and `clipboard-repro.log` in the evidence directory. The apparent empty-grid problem was traced to the test's detached source state; all four filter combinations passed after restoring it.

## Earlier desktop attempt and observation limits

Build: Debug x64 solution build succeeded with 0 warnings / 0 errors (root verified the final Build.log). Windows Terminal 1.24.11911.0 was started through the repository's interactive wrapper and showed process title `Complete Control Showcase (TUI)`; the target window was absent from sky's target inventory and `sky.launch_app` returned the exact rejection `product policy blocks this app: C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_1.24.11911.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe\WindowsTerminal.exe`. The task-owned TUI process (PID 14276), its PowerShell host (PID 36716), and Windows Terminal (PID 28352) were force-stopped after the rejection. This forced cleanup does not establish the SOP's normal-exit/terminal-restoration checks. Profile settings, live viewport, displayed colors/font/cursor, and physical keyboard/mouse input were not observed.

Independent bounded fallback: the documented `copilotExecute.ps1 -Interactive` wrapper ran in an exec-managed pseudoterminal (session 15079). The VT output and keyboard stream supported the List/TextList and local Ctrl+Q checks above. This is console replay evidence only; it is not attributed to Windows Terminal or physical input. The PTY child PID 28872 was force-stopped after no reliable route to the Exit page was available; wrapper session 15079 ended with exit code 1 and emitted `ESC[?9001l`, `ESC[?1004l` and `ESC[m`. That is forced cleanup, not a normal exit.
